details.description: Sonic-3.5 is Cartesia's text-to-speech model for low-latency, multilingual voice agents, reporting sub-90ms time-to-first-audio latency. It natively supports 42 languages and handles alphanumerics, order numbers, phone numbers, emails, and context-aware English heteronym pronunciation without requiring transcript preprocessing. Cartesia's docs note that its newer Sonic-3.6 model is now generally available, making Sonic-3.5 the prior generation in the Sonic line.
advantages: Sub-90ms time-to-first-audio latency, aimed at real-time voice agents.
Parses alphanumerics such as order numbers, phone numbers, IDs, and emails, and applies context-aware pronunciation for English heteronyms (e.g. 'read', 'bass', 'bow') without manual preprocessing.
Scores an Elo of 1185 (rank #13) on Artificial Analysis's Provider Voice speech arena leaderboard.
disadvantages: Superseded within Cartesia's own lineup: the docs point users to Sonic-3.6, now generally available, as the newest model.
No voice cloning, Custom Pronunciation Dictionaries, or fine-grained emotion/style control is documented on the model-specific Sonic-3.5 page.
use_cases: Customer support and agent call transcripts read aloud.
Multilingual voice products needing native-quality delivery across 42 languages.
Reading structured data such as phone numbers, order IDs, and emails aloud accurately.

notes: Voice cloning ('clone any voice with 10 seconds of audio') is described on Cartesia's general Sonic product page, not on the Sonic-3.5-specific docs page, so I left it out of advantages rather than assume it applies unchanged to this exact snapshot.
